decisive_items: Linear moist, eroded, exophytic, condyloma-like plaques present in:- Bilateral submammary folds- Intergluteal cleft- Under the abdominal apron- Ulcers of the bilateral genitocrural folds- Vulvar edema
Family history notable for son with similar condition
Pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia  - Focal superficial erosion  - Superficial and deep granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate
response.rationale: The patient's clinical presentation of painful intertriginous wounds and characteristic skin lesions, along with a family history of a similar condition, is most consistent with hidradenitis suppurativa. The histopathology results also support this diagnosis, showing pseudoepitheliomatous epidermal hyperplasia and granulomatous inflammation.

rejected.why: Lack of specific clinical presentation and family history to support granulomatous dermatitis as the primary diagnosis
Negative colonoscopy results and lack of gastrointestinal symptoms make Crohn's disease less likely
Negative laboratory tests for infectious agents and lack of response to antibiotics make granuloma inguinale less likely
